# Radio

One option inside a radio group. Not usable on its own.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `radio` |
| Family | inputs |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | `state-layer` |

## Behavior

An option rendered by its group, with no primitive of its own. It holds no state: getRadioGroupProps decides whether this one is checked, whether it is the tab stop, and what happens when it is activated. That is the point — a radio that owned any of those could disagree with its siblings.

- **A Radio outside a RadioGroup is a mistake, not a fallback** — Alone it has no name to share, no siblings to be exclusive with, and no way to be reached by arrow keys — everything that makes it a radio lives in the group. Rendering one standalone would produce a control that looks right and behaves like nothing.
- **`value` is required and is the item's whole identity** — It is what the group compares against, what arrow keys walk, and what a form submits. Without it the group has no way to refer to this option.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | — | This option's value. What the group reports when it is chosen. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | The option's label. |
| `description?` | `ReactNode` | — | Helper text under the label, for an option whose consequence is not obvious. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks this one option while leaving it focusable and readable. |

### `value`

```ts
value: string
```

This option's value. What the group reports when it is chosen.

**Don't use for**

- Reusing a value across two radios in one group — the group would consider both chosen.

### `label`

```ts
label: ReactNode
```

The option's label.

**Accessibility** A real `<label for>`, so the text is part of the hit target.

### `description`

```ts
description?: ReactNode
```

Helper text under the label, for an option whose consequence is not obvious.

**Don't use for**

- Restating the label in more words.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks this one option while leaving it focusable and readable.

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-disabled`. Arrow keys still land on it; it just does not become the answer.

## Use cases

### Inside its group

The only correct use.

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Billing period" value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod}>
  <Radio value="annual" label="Annual" description="Two months free" />
</RadioGroup>
```

Everything that makes this a radio — the shared name, the exclusivity, the arrow-key reachability — comes from the group.
